papers.title: Field-ridge structured bioactive Zn-based scaffold promotes bone regeneration via cellular mechanotransduction.
papers.abstract: Large bone defects often exhibit impaired healing due to the absence of a favorable osteoinductive microenvironment at the defect core. Drawing inspiration from agricultural field-ridge structures, we developed a Zn-based metallic biomimetic scaffold, designated the "Osteogenic Conditioning Scaffold" (OCS), with a tailored porous architecture and groove-ridge-like surface texture to enhance bone conduction and osteogenesis. Using a rationally designed laser scanning strategy in laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF), we spatially regulated melt-track overlap to generate ordered groove-ridge-like textures, enabling the one-step fabrication of 3D-printed Zn-0.4Li porous scaffolds with oriented surface textures. In vitro evaluations revealed that the OCS promoted the adhesion and spreading of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), activated mechanotransduction signaling (upregulated VCL, phosphorylated FAK, and nuclear translocation of YAP), and triggered epigenetic regulator shifts (downregulated KDM5A and upregulated KDM6A), thereby enhancing osteogenic differentiation. In a rabbit critical-sized calvarial defect model, the scaffold significantly accelerated new bone formation and osseointegration, with consistent mechanistic signatures validated in vivo. This robust, stable, and readily tunable fabrication approach enables the synergistic integration of osteogenic bioactivity from Zn2+ and Li+ ions with the osteoinductive effects of hierarchical porous and groove-ridge-like textures, offering a promising strategy for the repair of large bone defects.

papers.title: Synergistic antibacterial and osteogenic properties of micro-arc oxidation GO@Ag/SF composite coatings for the repair of infectious bone defects.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration of titanium-based implants remain major clinical challenges. Conventional drug-loaded coatings often fail to simultaneously achieve long-term antibacterial activity and the construction of an osteogenic microenvironment. METHODS: In this study, a graphene oxide-supported silver nanoparticle/silk fibroin (GO@Ag/SF) composite coating was developed and modified via micro-arc oxidation. By precisely controlling the GO/AgNO3 volume ratio, the antibacterial and osteogenic performances of the coatings were systematically evaluated. A rat model of infectious bone defect was employed to verify the in vivo therapeutic efficacy. RESULTS: The optimized GO@Ag-2/SF coating exhibited pH-responsive sustained Ag+ release, with cumulative release increasing from 0.23 μg/mL under physiological conditions to 0.69 μg/mL under acidic conditions over 672 h. Under NIR irradiation, the coating reached 59.8°C within 10 min and achieved potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, with inhibition rates up to 98.3 ± 1.2%. The GO@Ag-2/SF coating also promoted osteogenic differentiation by enhancing ALP activity, collagen secretion, calcium mineralization, and the expression of RUNX-2, ALP, COL-I, and OCN. In vivo, GO@Ag-2/SF reduced inflammatory infiltration and improved peri-implant bone regeneration, with increased BIC, BV/TV, and Tb.Th and reduced Tb.Sp. Moreover, pull-out testing demonstrated the highest bone-implant mechanical fixation in the GO@Ag-2/SF group, confirming enhanced functional osseointegration in the infected bone defect model. CONCLUSION: Through the synergistic effects of its components, the GO@Ag/SF coating established a dynamic antibacterial-osteogenic balance, offering a promising strategy for the repair of infectious bone defects.

papers.title: Modeling Proliferative Versus Migratory Melanoma Cell Phenotypes Using Biofabricated Matrices.
papers.abstract: Biofabrication enables the controlled generation of three-dimensional cell cultures that can be highly useful to study different cellular phenotypes. As melanoma cells reveal high plasticity, and the "phenotype switching model" defining the cells as either proliferative or migratory active has been described, we recently developed a 3D bioprinted model mimicking these phenotypes. Here, we describe the generation of these bioprinted models based on either Matrigel or Cellink Bioink, which can be used with various cell lines and which allows for the analysis of cell response on microscopic and molecular levels. This model system offers novel opportunities for fundamental research and drug testing on heterogeneous tumors like melanoma.

papers.title: Comprehensive Full Mouth Rehabilitation Utilizing Dental Implants and Natural Teeth: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Edentulism poses significant functional, aesthetic, and psychological challenges, particularly in older patients and in regions where access to advanced surgical procedures may be limited.Full-mouth rehabilitation using dental implants is an effective treatment option; however, extensive implant placement and adjunctive surgical procedures are not always feasible.This case report describes a hybrid full-mouth rehabilitation approach combining implant-supported prostheses with the strategic retention of natural mandibular teeth.A 65-year-old male patient presented with complete maxillary edentulism and partial mandibular edentulism.Eight implants were placed in the maxilla and two implants in the mandible, while six remaining mandibular teeth were preserved through endodontic treatment and post-core restoration to support the final prosthesis.Digital imaging, cone-beam computed tomography, and guided treatment planning were used to optimize implant positioning and prosthetic design.The definitive restorations achieved stable osseointegration, satisfactory occlusion, improved mastication, and favorable aesthetic outcomes.The patient reported a marked improvement in oral function and quality of life during follow-up evaluations.This case highlights the clinical feasibility and benefits of a hybrid rehabilitation strategy that integrates dental implants with preserved natural teeth, reducing surgical complexity while maintaining functional and biomechanical stability.Such an approach may represent a practical and costeffective alternative for managing complex edentulism, particularly in patients with anatomical, medical, or resource-related limitations.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification of Energy Extraction in a Process of Carbon Sequestration in Fractured Reservoirs: A Coupled Heat Transfer Phase Transport Study
papers.abstract: Injecting CO2 into depleted oil and gas reservoirs is a cost-effective method for geological CO2 sequestration as these reservoirs commonly possess proven capacity and sealing structures, and require lower exploration costs. The extracted brine can also be utilized for various thermal purposes. The presence of both natural and induced fractures in depleted oil and gas reservoirs can significantly impact their capacity for CO2 sequestration and thermal exploitation. Accurate simulation of the multi-phase transport and heat transfer resulting from CO2 injection requires a clear definition of properties for both the fracture and porous media. However, estimation of these properties, especially those of fractures, can be challenging and subject to significant uncertainty. This paper evaluates the extent to which uncertainty in fracture and matrix parameters affects simulated flow and transport results and the associated CO2 sequestration and geothermal energy extraction metrics. This is done through Monte Carlo-based uncertainty propagation analysis and Sobol-based global sensitivity analysis. Polynomial chaos expansions are used to analyze continuous changes of response variables with variations in the input parameters within a reasonable computational time. The effect of uncertainty in fracture length, aperture and rotation angle, longitudinal and transverse dispersivity, reservoir permeability and anisotropy, and the van Genuchten-Mualem parameters are assessed. Based on the results, these parameters are ranked according to their influence on the mass of stored CO2, reservoir heat loss, brine-based heat flux in the production well, and a measure of the CO2 travel time.

papers.title: Active delta-learning for surface hopping: efficient fitting of potential energy surfaces
papers.abstract: Active learning has become central to modern machine-learning workflows for trajectory surface hopping, enabling automatic construction of training sets for excited-state potentials. However, currently used protocols can struggle with convergence, requiring large datasets and extensive human intervention. Here, we combine active learning with Δ-learning - where the ML model predicts the difference between a target quantum chemical method and a computationally efficient baseline - into an end-to-end protocol for active delta-learning (ADL) of potential energy surfaces for trajectory surface hopping dynamics. The protocol is tested on a benchmark system, fulvene, where a twofold data efficiency is achieved with respect to fine-tuning from a pre-trained foundational model, OMNI-P2x. Next, we analyze the case of PSB4, a protonated Schiff base with multiple competing torsional deactivation channels. Here, pure ML active learning fails to converge despite extensive sampling of over 14 000 points, while ADL converges within just two iterations and 900 sampled points, yielding good agreement with the reference.

papers.title: Developing an Artificial Intelligence Course for a Small Undergraduate Program
papers.abstract: This paper presents the systematic design and development of an undergraduate artificial intelligence and machine learning course intended to serve both technical and non-technical students in higher education. The work addresses growing industry demand for AI and ML competencies by proposing a comprehensive course framework that accommodates students from diverse academic backgrounds while maintaining academic rigor. Building upon established experiential and active learning theories, the proposed course design emphasizes hands-on learning through progressive skill development. The curriculum incorporates fundamental concepts including supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, natural language processing, and computer vision, while integrating ethical considerations throughout. The pedagogical framework utilizes cloud-based laboratory environments and industry-standard tools to provide accessible yet rigorous learning experiences that bridge theoretical understanding with practical implementation skills. This pedagogical design case synthesizes current best practices in AI and ML education, drawing from successful data analytics program implementations to develop a comprehensive framework for course design.

papers.title: Preventing Periprosthetic Femur Fractures in Total Hip Arthroplasty: How to Choose a Femoral Component in 2026.
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic femur fracture (PFF) is a dreaded complication following primary total hip arthroplasty, often requiring reoperation and increased utilization of resources, and is frequently associated with poor patient outcomes. Historically, cemented femoral stems have consistently outperformed noncemented femoral stems in terms of PFF prevention. However, in the past 5 years, the use of triple-taper collared noncemented stems has been associated with PFF protection, potentially narrowing the gap in risk profile between cemented and noncemented femoral stems. The objective is to provide surgeons a contemporary framework for selecting the best femoral THA components according to patient anatomy, demographics, and previous surgeries. It is important to review current literature on cemented femoral stem outcomes, including a discussion of different cemented stem designs, as well as comparison of triple-taper collared stems with cemented and other noncemented options in terms of PFF risk. Furthermore, it is important to evaluate the indication for modular or custom stems and review techniques for managing intraoperative PFFs.

papers.title: Evaluation of Ongoing Pain After Successful Hip Arthroplasty.
papers.abstract: It is important to provide a systematic framework for evaluating continued pain after a total hip arthroplasty, first ruling out prosthesis-related causes such as infection, loosening, malposition, and instability, before providing an overview of extra-articular pain contributors. There are three major extra-articular areas of pain: iliopsoas pathology presenting as anterior groin pain, abductor dysfunction and offset abnormalities contributing to lateral hip pain, and sacroiliac joint and proximal hamstring pathology as drivers of posterior hip pain. It is important to outline the relevant diagnostic and treatment strategies along with their associated outcomes. Adopting a structured diagnostic approach and maintaining an awareness of various extra-articular causes of pain can improve diagnostic accuracy and avoid any unnecessary interventions while optimizing patient recovery.

papers.title: AdamW-Reptile Based Adaptive Stochastic Physics-Informed Neural Network for Remaining Useful Life Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical in prognostics and health management (PHM) but remains challenging under noisy measurements, limited run-to-failure labels, and changing operating conditions. To address these issues, this study proposes the AdamW–Reptile based Adaptive Stochastic Physics-Informed Neural Network (AR-ASPINN) for RUL prediction. Time Context-Aware Transformer (TCAT) extracts long-range degradation representations from multivariate sensor sequences. An Adaptive Stochastic Physics-Informed Loss Function (ASPILF) is then introduced to combine a physics-guided deterministic degradation-dynamics residual with SDE-based stochastic perturbations, where a dynamic weighting strategy progressively shifts training from stochastic degradation regularization toward deterministic degradation consistency. AdamW–Reptile meta-learning learns a transferable initialization for rapid few-shot adaptation. AR-ASPINN achieves an average Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 12.05 on Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) and an RMSE of 0.0396 ± 0.0064 under few-shot adaptation on the laboratory gearbox dataset, demonstrating improved accuracy, robustness, and cross-condition adaptability.

papers.title: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Dispatch of Microgrids
papers.abstract: To address the challenges of incomplete state representation, hard-to-guarantee safety constraints, and slow convergence driven by sparse rewards in microgrid dispatch, a knowledge graph-enhanced deep reinforcement learning (DRL) optimization method is proposed. Based on the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) framework, the approach integrates both static dispatch regulation and event knowledge graphs. Specifically, a Relational Graph Convolutional Network (R-GCN) is deployed to encode the static graph into the state space, thereby enhancing structural and semantic awareness of the system. To enhance operational safety, rule reasoning over the static knowledge graph formulates a safe action feasible region, where projection operators ensure strict satisfaction of device-level box constraints, while coupled constraints are addressed via reward penalties. Furthermore, event graph similarity retrieval is leveraged to construct potential-based reward shaping and adaptive behavioral regularization, which are combined with a knowledge-credibility-weighted experience replay mechanism to accelerate convergence. Simulation results on a modified IEEE 33-bus system across four distinct scenarios demonstrate that, compared to the baseline SAC algorithm in conventional settings, the proposed method reduces daily operational costs by 7.8%, lowers constraint violation rates by 81.3%, and decreases convergence episodes by 33.6% on this benchmark. Moreover, it exhibits superior robustness and performance across all metrics under complex perturbation scenarios.

papers.title: Transformer-Enhanced Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning for Simulation-Based Autonomous Spot-Welding Control of Robotic Manipulators
papers.abstract: This study presents a Transformer-Enhanced Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning framework for simulation-based control of sequential robotic spot-welding tasks. The method couples a shared temporal encoder with deterministic actor-critic learning, auxiliary safety and process-quality outputs, and a multi-objective reward for position, force, smoothness, energy, time, collision, and safety objectives. In the reported simulations against Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), the proposed configuration reached an average reward of 1268.9, a task success rate of 98.8%, a positioning error of 0.96 mm, a contact-force Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 24.3 N, and a simulation-derived process-quality proxy of 0.94. A controlled 2 × 2 ablation separates the effects of the temporal encoder and reward formulation; both factors improve the descriptive metrics, although their interaction is sub-additive for several outcomes. The available record does not contain raw multi-seed data, authenticated physical trials, complete implementation hyperparameters, or instrumented latency and memory logs. Accordingly, no inferential-significance, metallurgical weld-quality, real-time, or hardware-feasibility claim is made. The contribution is therefore a simulation-based sequence-aware control formulation whose physical deployment requires independently documented validation.

papers.title: Hybrid Vehicular Cluster Control Model Based on Transformer-Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) are capable of substantially enhancing roadway safety and traffic throughput in hybrid driving environments. To address the challenges of cluster control and validation testing for intelligent connected vehicles, a vehicular cluster control method and a multi-domain controller-in-the-loop simulation testing approach for hybrid driving environments are proposed in this paper. First, a unified modeling framework for the vehicular cluster control system is established by constructing a multiple-predecessor multiple-leader following topology, a variable time headway strategy, and a dynamics model of hybrid vehicular clusters. Second, a multi-agent reinforcement learning-based vehicular cluster control model is developed using a hierarchical Transformer framework to dynamically characterize multi-layer cluster states. Hybrid vehicular cluster control is achieved through a shared-parameter multi-head Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) algorithm. Finally, the proposed Transformer-Double Deep Q-Network (Trans-DDQN) control model is deployed on domain controllers via model pruning and quantization techniques. A multi-domain controller-in-the-loop simulation testing system is constructed based on PreScan/MATLAB, incorporating a driving simulator to replicate hybrid driving scenarios. The final experimental validation demonstrates that, compared with the traditional Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Layered Conventional Double Deep Q-Network (LC-DDQN) model, the proposed method achieves markedly faster acceleration convergence than LC-DDQN, reduces the maximum inter-vehicle spacing deviation by 3.1% and 7.3% relative to LC-DDQN and MPC, and raises the minimum time to collision (TTC) from 1.9 to 5.0 s. These results indicate that the Trans-DDQN effectively enhances the operational stability of vehicular clusters and ensures consistent speed, acceleration, and spacing control.
